& \Rightarrow m=2

\]

questions.question:
Identify the correct statements about alkali metals

(A) The order of standard reduction potential \(\left( M ^{+} \mid M \right)\) for alkali metal ions is \(Na > Rb > Li\).
(B) CsI is highly soluble in water.
(C) Lithium carbonate is highly stable to heat.
(D) Potassium dissolved in concentrated liquid ammonia is blue in colour and paramagnetic.
(E) All the alkali metal hydrides are ionic solids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation:
(A) The order of standard reduction potential (\(M^+ \mid M\)) for alkali metal ions is \(\text{Na} > \text{Rb} > \text{Li}\): This statement is correct. The standard reduction potential values are roughly \(-2.71\text{ V}\) for \(\text{Na}\), \(-2.98\text{ V}\) for \(\text{Rb}\), and \(-3.04\text{ V}\) for \(\text{Li}\). Due to the exceptionally high hydration energy of the small \(\text{Li}^{+}\) ion, lithium has the most negative reduction potential, putting it at the bottom of this sequence. 

B)CsI is less soluble in water due to smaller hydration enthalpy of it's two ions
C) \(Li _2 CO _3\) is not so stable to heat and gets converted into \(Li _2 O\) and \(CO _2\).
D) Potassium dissolved in concentrated liquid ammonia is blue in colour and paramagnetic: This statement is incorrect. While dilute solutions of alkali metals in liquid ammonia are blue and paramagnetic due to free ammoniated electrons, concentrated solutions change to a copper-bronze color and become diamagnetic due to electron pairing

E) All the alkali metal hydrides are ionic solid (True).

questions.question:
Let \(f\) be a differentiable function defined on \(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) such that \(f(x)>0\) and \(f(x)+\int_0^x f(t) \sqrt{1-\left(\log _e f(t)\right)^2} d t=e, \forall x \in\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) then \(\left(6 \log _e f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)^2\) is equal to ___________.

 

[JEE Main 2023, 24 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
\(f(x)+\int_0^x f(t) \sqrt{1-\left(\log _e f(t)\right)^2} d t=e\)

Put \(x=0\)
\(\Rightarrow f(0)=e\)

Using leibnitz theorem
\(f^{\prime}(x)+f(x) \sqrt{1-(\ln f(x))^2}=0\)

Let, \(f(x)=y\)
\( \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=-y \sqrt{1-(\ln y)^2} \)
\( \Rightarrow \int \frac{d y}{y \sqrt{1-(\ln y)^2}}=-\int d x\)

Put \(\ln y=t\)
\(\Rightarrow \int \frac{d t}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}=-x+C\)

\( \Rightarrow \sin ^{-1} t=-x+C\) 

\(\Rightarrow \sin ^{-1}(\ln y)=-x+C \)

\( \Rightarrow \sin ^{-1}(\ln f(x))=-x+C \)

 But \( f(0)=e\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}=C\)

So, \(\sin ^{-1}(\ln f(x))=-x+\frac{\pi}{2}\)
Put \(x=\frac{\pi}{6}\)
\( \Rightarrow \sin ^{-1}\left(\ln f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)=\frac{-\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{2} \)
\( \Rightarrow \sin ^{-1}\left(\ln f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)=\frac{\pi}{3} \)
\( \Rightarrow \ln f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)

Hence, \(\left(6 \log _e f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)^2=\left(6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2=27\)

so put \(x=0\) in both equations.

From \((\lambda+1)x+\lambda y=4\),

From \(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y+\lambda=0\),

The orthocentre is \(H=(1,2)\).

The slope of \(AB\) is \(-\dfrac{3}{2}\),

so the altitude \(CH\) has slope \(\dfrac{2}{3}\).

\(CH:y-2=\dfrac{2}{3}(x-1)\)

Also, \(C\) lies on \(AC\),

so \(y=2x+2\)

\(2x+2-2=\dfrac{2}{3}(x-1)\)

\(2x=\dfrac{2}{3}x-\dfrac{2}{3}\)

\(\dfrac{4}{3}x=-\dfrac{2}{3}\)

\(\therefore C=\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},1\right)\)

For \(y^2=6x\),

\(a=\dfrac{3}{2}\),

and the tangent at parameter \(t\) is \(ty=x+\dfrac{3}{2}t^2\).
